outcome: false positive on newborn hearing screening (otoacoustic emissions test)
cohort: The study evaluated 2784 infants undergoing newborn hearing screening.
finding: False-positive rates in newborn hearing screening were significantly higher in public hospitals compared to private hospitals, and the rate decreased with increased screening age in private hospitals but not in public hospitals.
mod_finding: The false-positive rate in the first screening test was significantly higher in vaginal delivery compared to cesarean delivery, and this rate significantly decreased with screening age only in cesarean delivery.
cross-section timing: Performed before hospital discharge, based on screening age.
